solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: “Giant-killer” chants circling large pitch (10)

indicatorNotes.circling: SINGS goes round L, holding it inside

blocks.note: to chant is to sing
L = large, the clothing-size abbreviation
a musical pitch is a tone

annotation.surface: A football crowd chanting at a giant-killing underdog as they circle a big pitch.
annotation.walkthrough: In football a giant-killer is a small club beating a big one, and chants and pitch all fit that stadium; the real giant-killer is David's slingstone that felled Goliath.
annotation.definitionFit: The stone from David's sling killed the giant Goliath.

entries.clue: Ladies’ man, after ET’s demise, gets upset (3)

annotation.definitionNote: Ladies’ is short for the ladies’ room, a noun like LAV

indicatorNotes.after ET’s demise: ET dies out of VALET, leaving VAL
indicatorNotes.gets upset: in a down clue, upset turns the letters upside down, so VAL reads LAV

blocks.note: a gentleman's man is his valet
VALET without ET

annotation.surface: A ladies' man who is upset because ET has died.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Ladies’ man' reads as a womaniser, but the definition stops at the apostrophe: the ladies’ is a women's toilet, and LAV is short for lavatory.
annotation.definitionFit: The ladies’ is a public lavatory for women, and a lav is a lavatory.

entries.clue: Coppers chasing one-over-the-eight idiot … (9)

annotation.definitionNote: from the phrase 'ninepence in the shilling', said of someone not quite all there

blocks.note: one more than eight is nine
copper coins are pennies

annotation.surface: Police officers chasing a drunken fool, the story running on into the next clue.
annotation.walkthrough: 'One over the eight' is British slang for drunk and 'coppers' for police, so this reads as a pub chase. An old shilling was twelve pence, so someone only ninepence in the shilling is short of the full amount.
annotation.definitionFit: Someone 'ninepence in the shilling' lacks a quarter of their wits, an old British way of calling someone simple.

entries.clue: … after function collared Conservative (5)

indicatorNotes.collared: SINE takes hold of C, as a collar goes round a neck

blocks.note: sine is a trigonometric function
C = Conservative

annotation.surface: Continuing 3 down: the drunken idiot was chased after a party function where he grabbed a Tory.
annotation.walkthrough: The dots join this to 3 down so 'collared' reads as an arrest by the coppers there. 'Function' is maths, not a party.
annotation.definitionFit: 'Since then' and 'after that' say the same thing.

entries.clue: Underworld figure old pusher sorted out (7)

indicatorNotes.sorted out: the letters are put into a new order

blocks.note: O = old
anagram fodder

annotation.surface: A gangland boss dealing with a former drug dealer.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Underworld' and 'pusher' suggest organised crime; the underworld here is Hades, which Orpheus entered to fetch Eurydice.
annotation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Orpheus went down into the underworld to bring back his wife.

entries.clue: Expel priest that’s popular in China (9)

indicatorNotes.in: 'in' as a plain preposition: IN sits within MATE, the way something is in a box

blocks.note: Eli, the priest who raised Samuel in the Bible
what is popular is in
china = mate, from rhyming slang 'china plate'

annotation.surface: A priest thrown out for being liked in China.
annotation.walkthrough: The capital C makes China look like the country; it is Cockney rhyming slang, china plate = mate, a friend.
annotation.definitionFit: To eliminate someone is to expel them from a contest or group.

entries.clue: Chef half-heartedly eating up cold chicken (4)

indicatorNotes.half-heartedly: one of COOK's two middle O's goes, leaving COK
indicatorNotes.eating up: COK takes C inside it, as food goes in

blocks.note: COOK losing half its heart, one O
C = cold, as on a tap

annotation.surface: A half-hearted chef finishing off some cold chicken.
annotation.walkthrough: Chicken is both the dish in the surface and the definition; a cock is a male chicken.
annotation.definitionFit: A relation of kind: the male bird of the domestic chicken is called a cock.

entries.clue: Energy source bachelor discovered in motors (5)

indicatorNotes.discovered in: to be discovered in a place is to be found inside it, so B turns up within CARS

blocks.note: motors are cars
B = bachelor, as in BA

annotation.surface: A bachelor's energy source turns out to be the car engine.
annotation.walkthrough: Motors and energy point to fuel and engines; the energy source is the carbohydrates in food.
annotation.definitionFit: Carbohydrates, carbs for short, are the body's main source of energy.

entries.clue: Sweetener a court arranged with grass (6,5)

indicatorNotes.arranged: the letters are set in a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder
anagram fodder, joined by 'with'

annotation.surface: A sweetener for a court case, arranged with an informer.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sweetener' and 'grass' suggest a bribe for a police informer; British 'grass' means one. Castor sugar is British for superfine sugar.
annotation.definitionFit: Castor sugar is finely ground sugar used to sweeten baking.

entries.clue: Sadly, I’m no persevering late bloomer (7,8)

indicatorNotes.Sadly: the letters are in a sorry, disordered state

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 15 letters

annotation.surface: Someone lamenting that they gave up too soon and only developed late in life.
annotation.walkthrough: A late bloomer is usually a person who succeeds late; here it is a flower that opens in the evening.
annotation.definitionFit: The evening primrose opens its flowers late in the day.

entries.clue: Spot politician visiting Chequers, say (6)

indicatorNotes.visiting: MP goes inside PILE, as a guest goes into a house
indicatorNotes.say: Chequers is one example of a pile

blocks.note: a pile is a grand house, and Chequers is one
MP = Member of Parliament

annotation.surface: Spotting an MP on a visit to Chequers, the Prime Minister's country house.
annotation.walkthrough: Chequers is the British Prime Minister's country residence, and a pile is slang for a large stately house.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a spot on the face and a pimple are the same blemish.

entries.clue: Fancy priests in India with lace headwear? (7,4)

blocks.note: I = India in the phonetic alphabet
the Magi were Zoroastrian priests
net is a lacy mesh fabric
a hat is headwear

annotation.surface: Priests in India wearing fancy lace hats.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fancy' looks like an adjective for the hats; it is the exclamation 'Fancy!', meaning well I never.
annotation.definitionFit: 'Fancy that!' and 'Imagine that!' both express surprise.

entries.clue: English ministry for energy on the way out? (8)

blocks.note: E = English
a mission is a religious ministry

annotation.surface: A government department for energy that is about to be abolished.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Ministry' reads as a government department; it is the work of missionaries. 'On the way out' means going out, not dying.
annotation.definitionFit: The definition glosses the word's roots: to emit is to send out, and heat or light given off is the classic case.

entries.clue: Books of plants (7)

blocks.note: yearly publications, such as the hardback comic books British children get at Christmas
plants that complete their life cycle within one year

annotation.walkthrough: 'Of' makes it read as a book about plants, but it only joins two meanings: yearly books and one-season plants.
annotation.surface: Botany books.
annotation.definitionFit: Both a yearly book and a one-season plant are annuals.

entries.clue: Johnny Rotten supposedly was one in charts with a hit (9)

blocks.note: anagram fodder
anagram fodder

annotation.surface: Punk singer Johnny Rotten topping the charts with a hit record.
annotation.walkthrough: Johnny Rotten of the Sex Pistols sang 'I am an antichrist, I am an anarchist' in Anarchy in the UK, a charting hit, so the whole surface stays on topic.
annotation.definitionFit: Rotten proclaimed himself an anarchist in the Sex Pistols' first single.

entries.clue: Catch a break in detention (6)

blocks.note: to catch a suspect, as the police do
a halt or stoppage in a process, the medical sense when a heart stops
the state of being held by police

annotation.surface: A prisoner getting a lucky break while locked up.
annotation.walkthrough: 'A break' looks like a stroke of luck or an escape; it is a stoppage, the sense in cardiac arrest.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: police catch a suspect by arresting them, and an arrest is also a stop or break in a process.

entries.clue: Excited outburst bishop suppressed in power shower? (9)

indicatorNotes.suppressed: B is held back and left out

blocks.note: a brainstorm is a sudden excited outburst
B = bishop, the chess notation; this is removed

annotation.surface: A bishop losing his temper in a high-pressure bathroom shower.
annotation.walkthrough: A power shower is a bathroom fitting; the question mark lets it mean a powerful shower of rain.
annotation.definitionFit: A rainstorm is a shower with real force behind it.

entries.clue: Pictures porcine masseuse puts up (6)

indicatorNotes.puts up: the phrase gives the answer lodging inside it

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of 'porcine' and the start of 'masseuse'

annotation.surface: Photos of a pig-like masseuse hanging on the wall.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pictures' and 'puts up' suggest hanging photos; the pictures are the movies, and 'puts up' means houses.
annotation.definitionFit: Going to the pictures means going to the cinema.

entries.clue: Don’t start indiscriminate blubbing (7)

indicatorNotes.Don’t start: the first letter is not used

blocks.note: a sweeping statement is indiscriminate
SWEEPING without its S

annotation.surface: Someone told not to start crying at random.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Don't start' is what you say to someone about to cry, and here it instructs the solver.
annotation.definitionFit: Blubbing is British slang for crying, weeping.

entries.clue: Struggle with support if leader’s lacking (7)

blocks.note: W = with
a trestle is a support; without its T

annotation.surface: Someone struggling without support when there is no one to lead.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Leader' looks like a person in charge; it is the leading letter of TRESTLE.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, the physical grappling sense stretched to any effortful struggle.

entries.clue: Leader with long excuse for prorogation of Congress? (8)

blocks.note: a head is a leader
to ache for something is to long for it

annotation.surface: A political leader asking to suspend the legislature.
annotation.walkthrough: Congress looks like the US legislature; with the question mark it is sexual congress, and 'not tonight, I've got a headache' is the classic excuse for putting it off.
annotation.definitionFit: A headache is the stock excuse for postponing sex.

entries.clue: Pacifist punched by Republican gets teed off (5)

indicatorNotes.punched by: a punch lands inside its target, so DOVE is broken into by R

blocks.note: a dove is a pacifist
R = Republican

annotation.surface: A peace campaigner, hit by a Republican, is annoyed.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Teed off' reads as angry; in golf, teeing off is driving the ball from the tee.
annotation.definitionFit: A golfer who teed off drove the ball off the tee.

entries.clue: Maroon sweet a son polished off (6)

indicatorNotes.polished off: the S is finished off and removed

blocks.note: a sweet is a pudding, a dessert
S = son; one S is removed

annotation.surface: A maroon-coloured pudding that a son has eaten up.
annotation.walkthrough: Maroon looks like a colour next to 'sweet'; it is the verb, to strand someone.
annotation.definitionFit: To maroon someone is to desert them, leaving them stranded.

entries.clue: Live comfortably under Dad’s leadership (5)

indicatorNotes.leadership: only the first letter of Dad is taken
indicatorNotes.under: in a down clue what is under comes below, so WELL sits beneath D

blocks.note: first letter of Dad
to live well is to live comfortably

annotation.surface: Living comfortably under Dad's roof and rules.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Dad’s leadership' reads as living under a father's rule; it only takes Dad's leading letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, slightly formal: where you reside is where you live.

entries.clue: When and how to litter horses about to leave the field? (5,2,3,5)

blocks.clueFragment: When and how to litter horses
blocks.note: the surface reading: horses 'throw', or give birth to, foals, so this asks when and in what they are delivered
the meant reading: on the point of quitting a contest

annotation.surface: A question about when and how to spread litter for horses.
annotation.walkthrough: Horses 'throw' foals, so the first half plays on the phrase literally; the whole means to give up, from a boxer's corner throwing a towel into the ring.
annotation.definitionFit: To throw in the towel is to concede and quit the contest.

entries.clue: Organ one heard on the radio (3)

indicatorNotes.heard on the radio: on the radio you only hear the word

blocks.note: one is the Roman-numeral letter I, a single letter that sounds like the organ's name

annotation.surface: An organ piece heard played on the radio.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Organ' suggests the musical instrument on air; it is the body part.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: the organ of sight is one of the body's organs.

entries.clue: Some nasty, erupting red swelling (4)

indicatorNotes.Some: only part of the phrase is used

blocks.note: the letters straddle the end of 'nasty' and the first letter of 'erupting'

annotation.surface: A nasty red swelling breaking out.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface describes the answer itself, so it stays in the scene.
annotation.definitionFit: A stye is a red, swollen infection on the eyelid.

entries.clue: Helmet and arms distributed in prison (3,7)

indicatorNotes.distributed: the letters are spread out afresh

blocks.note: anagram fodder, joined by 'and'

annotation.surface: Riot gear and weapons handed out inside a prison.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Arms' reads as weapons but only lends its letters; the slammer is slang for jail.
annotation.definitionFit: The slammer is slang for prison, where doors slam shut.
